paragraphs.title: The famine and the demand to return to Egypt

easy.question: What was severe in the land?
answers: The famine
The rain
The peace
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The famine was severe in the land.”

easy.question: What did the father ask his sons to do?
answers: Go down to the sea
Return to Egypt and buy food
Stay at home
easy.explanation: Their father told them, “Go again, buy us a little food.”

easy.question: Who spoke to and answered their father?
answers: Reuben
Joseph
Judah
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “And Judah spoke unto him.”

medium.question: Why did Judah say they could not go down to Egypt without their brother?
answers: The man in Egypt had warned them not to see him without their brother
The food in Egypt was already gone
The road to Egypt was closed
medium.explanation: Judah reminded them that the man in Egypt had said they would not see him unless their brother was with them.

medium.question: In the phrase “Go again, buy us a little food,” what does “buy” mean?
answers: Break the vessels
Purchase food
Distribute the food
medium.explanation: The context shows that their father wanted them to obtain food from Egypt.

medium.question: What would happen if their father did not send their brother with them?
answers: They would remain in Egypt
They would bring different food
They would not go down to Egypt
medium.explanation: Judah said plainly, “If thou wilt not send him, we will not go down.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “when they had eaten up the corn”?
answers: The food they brought from Egypt was gone
They refused to eat the food
They had not yet reached Egypt
challenge.explanation: “Eaten up” indicates that the food they brought had run out, so they needed to return to Egypt.

challenge.question: What central difficulty faced Jacob’s sons in these verses?
answers: They had no father to lead them
They needed food but had to take their brother with them
They did not know where Egypt was
challenge.explanation: The famine forced them to obtain food, but the ruler in Egypt would not receive them without their brother.

challenge.question: Why did Judah repeat the man’s words in verse 5?
answers: To change his condition
To show that the man had forgotten his words
To stress that they could not go to Egypt without their brother
challenge.explanation: Repeating the condition strengthened Judah’s argument that they could not see the man or buy food without their brother.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “when they had eaten up the corn”?
answers: The food they brought from Egypt was gone
They refused to eat the food
They had not yet reached Egypt
questions.explanation: “Eaten up” indicates that the food they brought had run out, so they needed to return to Egypt.

questions.question: What central difficulty faced Jacob’s sons in these verses?
answers: They had no father to lead them
They needed food but had to take their brother with them
They did not know where Egypt was
questions.explanation: The famine forced them to obtain food, but the ruler in Egypt would not receive them without their brother.

questions.question: Why did Judah repeat the man’s words in verse 5?
answers: To change his condition
To show that the man had forgotten his words
To stress that they could not go to Egypt without their brother
questions.explanation: Repeating the condition strengthened Judah’s argument that they could not see the man or buy food without their brother.

paragraphs.title: Jacob suffers and his sons explain

easy.question: What did Israel complain to his sons about?
answers: That they had harmed him by telling the man they had a brother
That they had sold all the grain
That they had not asked about their father
easy.explanation: Israel was upset because they had told the man that they had another brother.

easy.question: Who asked Jacob’s sons whether they had a brother?
answers: Their father, Israel
The man in Egypt
One of their brothers
easy.explanation: The man had asked them, “Have ye another brother?”

easy.question: What did the brothers tell the man?
answers: That their father was dead
That they had no family
That their father was alive and they had a brother
easy.explanation: They answered that their father was alive and said that they had a brother.

medium.question: Why did Israel think his sons had harmed him?
answers: They had told the man that they had a brother
They refused to go down to Egypt
They hid the grain from him
medium.explanation: Israel saw their disclosure as the cause of their trouble, because it led to questions about the brother.

medium.question: In “Why did you deal so ill with me?” what does “deal so ill” mean?
answers: Why did you make me happy?
Why did you cause me trouble or harm?
Why did you call me?
medium.explanation: In Israel’s complaint, the phrase means that they had caused him trouble.

medium.question: What was the sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Israel questioned the man, and the brothers went to Egypt
The brothers brought their brother, and then Israel questioned them
The man asked about their family, they answered, and then Israel complained
medium.explanation: The man asked about their father and brother; they answered, and afterward Israel complained.

challenge.question: What did the brothers mean by “according to the tenor of these words”?
answers: They answered according to the man’s questions
They spoke according to their father’s words
They answered without being asked anything
challenge.explanation: They explained that they had told the man about their father and brother in response to his questions.

challenge.question: What did the brothers mean by “Could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?”
answers: They knew in advance that he would demand their brother
They could not have known that his questions would lead to this demand
They had already brought their brother to Egypt
challenge.explanation: They argued that they could not have anticipated that the man would use their answers to demand their brother.

challenge.question: What is meant by “of our state, and of our kindred”?
answers: The man asked only where they lived
The man asked only about their father
The man asked about them and their family or ancestry
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to their condition and family background, showing that the man asked about them and their family.

questions.question: What did the brothers mean by “according to the tenor of these words”?
answers: They answered according to the man’s questions
They spoke according to their father’s words
They answered without being asked anything
questions.explanation: They explained that they had told the man about their father and brother in response to his questions.

questions.question: What did the brothers mean by “Could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?”
answers: They knew in advance that he would demand their brother
They could not have known that his questions would lead to this demand
They had already brought their brother to Egypt
questions.explanation: They argued that they could not have anticipated that the man would use their answers to demand their brother.

questions.question: What is meant by “of our state, and of our kindred”?
answers: The man asked only where they lived
The man asked only about their father
The man asked about them and their family or ancestry
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to their condition and family background, showing that the man asked about them and their family.

easy.question: Who spoke to his father Israel?
answers: Judah
Joseph
Reuben
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Judah said unto Israel his father.”

easy.question: Whom did Judah ask his father to send with him?
answers: Joseph
The lad
One of the servants
easy.explanation: Judah asked, “Send the lad with me.”

easy.question: What did Judah say would happen if they went?
answers: They would remain at home
They would fight Egypt
They would live and not die
easy.explanation: Judah said, “That we may live, and not die,” because they needed food.

medium.question: What was the result of delaying, according to Judah?
answers: They could already have returned twice
They lost all their money
They reached Egypt for the first time
medium.explanation: Judah said, “If we had not lingered, surely now we had returned this second time.”

medium.question: In “I will be surety for him,” what does “be surety” mean?
answers: Hide him
Take responsibility for him
Send him alone
medium.explanation: Judah pledged to be responsible for the lad’s safety and return.

medium.question: Why did Judah mention both their father and their little ones?
answers: To show that the famine affected the whole family
To say that they did not need food
To ask their father to leave alone
medium.explanation: Judah emphasized that everyone—the brothers, their father, and their children—could suffer if they did not act.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “that we may live, and not die” about the family’s condition?
answers: The family faced famine and danger
The family was celebrating a victory
The family had left Egypt
challenge.explanation: The contrast between living and dying shows that the family faced severe food shortages and danger.

challenge.question: What did Judah mean by “of my hand shalt thou require him”?
answers: His father would ask him for money
His father would hold him accountable if the lad did not return
The lad would ask him for permission to go
challenge.explanation: Judah promised that if he did not bring the lad back, his father could demand an account from him.

challenge.question: What cause-and-effect relationship did Judah present?
answers: If the lad went, they could obtain food and live
If the lad stayed, they would immediately return to Egypt
If Judah stayed, the family would not be hungry
challenge.explanation: Judah connected sending the lad to Egypt with obtaining food and surviving the famine.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “that we may live, and not die” about the family’s condition?
answers: The family faced famine and danger
The family was celebrating a victory
The family had left Egypt
questions.explanation: The contrast between living and dying shows that the family faced severe food shortages and danger.

questions.question: What did Judah mean by “of my hand shalt thou require him”?
answers: His father would ask him for money
His father would hold him accountable if the lad did not return
The lad would ask him for permission to go
questions.explanation: Judah promised that if he did not bring the lad back, his father could demand an account from him.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect relationship did Judah present?
answers: If the lad went, they could obtain food and live
If the lad stayed, they would immediately return to Egypt
If Judah stayed, the family would not be hungry
questions.explanation: Judah connected sending the lad to Egypt with obtaining food and surviving the famine.

paragraphs.title: Gifts, money, and Benjamin go to Egypt

easy.question: What did Israel ask his sons to take as a gift to the man in Egypt?
answers: The best products of the land
Silver and gold vessels
New clothing
easy.explanation: Israel told them to take some of the best produce of the land as a present.

easy.question: What did Israel command them to do with the money found in their sacks?
answers: Leave it at home
Return it and take additional money
Give it as a gift
easy.explanation: Israel thought the money might have been returned by mistake, so he told them to take it back and bring more money.

easy.question: Whom did the brothers take with them to Egypt?
answers: Joseph
Simeon alone
Benjamin
easy.explanation: The brothers took Benjamin, as Israel had instructed.

medium.question: Why did Israel tell his sons to take additional money?
answers: To buy new gifts
Perhaps the first money had been returned by mistake
To pay the man for Benjamin
medium.explanation: Israel suggested that the money returned in their sacks might have been an oversight.

medium.question: What did the brothers do after taking the gift, the money, and Benjamin?
answers: They returned home
They waited in Canaan
They went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph
medium.explanation: The verse says that they rose, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

medium.question: What does “a present” mean in “carry down the man a present”?
answers: A gift
A journey
A meal
medium.explanation: In this context, a present is a gift brought to someone.

challenge.question: What did Israel express by saying, “If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved”?
answers: He was sure his sons would return immediately
He was prepared to face the possibility of losing his children
He planned to remain in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Israel expressed grief and acceptance that he could not control the outcome, even if further loss came.

challenge.question: What happened between Israel’s instructions and the brothers’ actions?
answers: Israel asked them to take Benjamin, and they did so
Israel asked them to stay in the land, and they stayed
Israel asked them to send a gift, and they took nothing
challenge.explanation: Israel told them to take Benjamin and return to the man, and the brothers did exactly that.

challenge.question: Who were probably the “other brother” and Benjamin whom Israel asked the man to send?
answers: Joseph and Reuben
Judah and Levi
Simeon and Benjamin
challenge.explanation: The other brother was probably Simeon, who had remained in Egypt; Benjamin was the brother they brought.

questions.question: What did Israel express by saying, “If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved”?
answers: He was sure his sons would return immediately
He was prepared to face the possibility of losing his children
He planned to remain in Egypt
questions.explanation: Israel expressed grief and acceptance that he could not control the outcome, even if further loss came.

questions.question: What happened between Israel’s instructions and the brothers’ actions?
answers: Israel asked them to take Benjamin, and they did so
Israel asked them to stay in the land, and they stayed
Israel asked them to send a gift, and they took nothing
questions.explanation: Israel told them to take Benjamin and return to the man, and the brothers did exactly that.

questions.question: Who were probably the “other brother” and Benjamin whom Israel asked the man to send?
answers: Joseph and Reuben
Judah and Levi
Simeon and Benjamin
questions.explanation: The other brother was probably Simeon, who had remained in Egypt; Benjamin was the brother they brought.

easy.question: Whom did Joseph see with his brothers?
answers: Benjamin
Pharaoh
His father
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Joseph saw Benjamin with them.”

easy.question: What did Joseph command the ruler of his house to do?
answers: Send the men to Canaan
Bring the men home
Give them money
easy.explanation: Joseph told him, “Bring these men home.”

easy.question: When were the men supposed to eat with Joseph?
answers: At night
In the morning
At noon
easy.explanation: Joseph said, “These men shall dine with me at noon.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph saw Benjamin, ordered a feast, and the steward brought them into the house
The steward brought them in, and then Joseph saw Benjamin
The brothers ate, and then Joseph ordered them brought in
medium.explanation: First Joseph saw Benjamin, then gave the order, and finally the steward carried it out.

medium.question: Why did Joseph order a slaughter and a feast to be prepared?
answers: To sell them food
Because the men would eat with him at noon
To send them back
medium.explanation: Joseph explained his command by saying that the men would dine with him at noon.

medium.question: In “slay, and make ready,” what does “make ready” refer to?
answers: Preparing meat or a meal
Writing a letter
Guarding the house
medium.explanation: The words occur before the meal, so they refer to preparing food.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph ordering a feast immediately after seeing Benjamin?
answers: Seeing Benjamin was connected with the special invitation to the feast
Joseph did not want to see his brothers
Joseph intended to send Benjamin alone
challenge.explanation: The verses closely connect Joseph’s seeing Benjamin with his order to bring the men in and prepare a feast.

challenge.question: Who is “the man” in verse 17?
answers: Joseph
The ruler of Joseph’s house
Benjamin
challenge.explanation: It is the man whom Joseph commanded in the previous verse—the steward of his house.

challenge.question: What does “the man brought the men into Joseph’s house” show?
answers: The men remained in the field
The men ate with Jacob
The men were brought into Joseph’s home
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the steward brought them into Joseph’s house.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph ordering a feast immediately after seeing Benjamin?
answers: Seeing Benjamin was connected with the special invitation to the feast
Joseph did not want to see his brothers
Joseph intended to send Benjamin alone
questions.explanation: The verses closely connect Joseph’s seeing Benjamin with his order to bring the men in and prepare a feast.

questions.question: Who is “the man” in verse 17?
answers: Joseph
The ruler of Joseph’s house
Benjamin
questions.explanation: It is the man whom Joseph commanded in the previous verse—the steward of his house.

questions.question: What does “the man brought the men into Joseph’s house” show?
answers: The men remained in the field
The men ate with Jacob
The men were brought into Joseph’s home
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the steward brought them into Joseph’s house.

paragraphs.title: The brothers fear because of the money

easy.question: What did the brothers fear when they were brought into Joseph’s house?
answers: That they would be taken as slaves
That they would find no food
That Joseph would flee from them
easy.explanation: They feared that the money would be used against them and that they and their donkeys would be taken as slaves.

easy.question: To whom did the brothers speak about the money?
answers: Joseph himself
The steward of Joseph’s house
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: They approached the steward of Joseph’s house at the doorway.

easy.question: What did the brothers find in their sacks at the inn?
answers: More bread
A letter from Joseph
The money they had paid
easy.explanation: They found their money in their sacks, although they did not know who had returned it.

medium.question: Why did the brothers think they had been brought into Joseph’s house?
answers: To accuse them over the money and take them as slaves
To invite them to a feast
To appoint them as officials
medium.explanation: They feared that the money in their sacks would lead Joseph’s officials to accuse and enslave them.

medium.question: What did the brothers do after discovering the money in their sacks?
answers: They left it at the inn
They brought it back with them
They used it to buy food
medium.explanation: They said, “We have brought it again in our hand.”

medium.question: What does “our sacks” mean in this passage?
answers: Our houses
Our bags or containers
Our donkeys
medium.explanation: The money was found inside the bags used to carry their goods.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers hurry to speak with the steward at the door?
answers: To explain the money before they were suspected
To ask him to join their journey
To tell him they did not want food
challenge.explanation: They feared suspicion, so they immediately explained that the money had appeared in their sacks without their knowledge.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the brothers tried to prove their honesty?
answers: They hid the money
They said they had returned the money and brought additional money
They refused to speak with Joseph’s men
challenge.explanation: They emphasized that they had returned the money found in their sacks and had brought more money to buy food.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “our money in full weight”?
answers: The money found was exactly the amount they had paid
The money was counterfeit
They did not know how much they had paid
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the money found was the full amount of their original payment.

questions.question: Why did the brothers hurry to speak with the steward at the door?
answers: To explain the money before they were suspected
To ask him to join their journey
To tell him they did not want food
questions.explanation: They feared suspicion, so they immediately explained that the money had appeared in their sacks without their knowledge.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the brothers tried to prove their honesty?
answers: They hid the money
They said they had returned the money and brought additional money
They refused to speak with Joseph’s men
questions.explanation: They emphasized that they had returned the money found in their sacks and had brought more money to buy food.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “our money in full weight”?
answers: The money found was exactly the amount they had paid
The money was counterfeit
They did not know how much they had paid
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the money found was the full amount of their original payment.

paragraphs.title: Reassurance, meeting Simeon, and preparing the feast

easy.question: Whom did the steward bring out to the brothers?
answers: Simeon
Joseph
Benjamin
easy.explanation: The verse says that the steward brought Simeon out to them.

easy.question: What did the steward give the brothers and their donkeys?
answers: Bread and clothing
Water and fodder
Money and gifts
easy.explanation: He gave the brothers water to wash their feet and fodder for their donkeys.

easy.question: What did the brothers prepare before Joseph came?
answers: The road
Their house
The present
easy.explanation: The verse says that they prepared the present until Joseph came.

medium.question: Why did the steward say, “Peace be to you, fear not”?
answers: He explained that their money had reached him and that God had given them treasure
Joseph had already left Egypt
Their donkey had been found
medium.explanation: He reassured them that he had received their money and that God had given them treasure in their sacks.

medium.question: What happened before the brothers prepared the present?
answers: Joseph ate with them
The steward gave them water and fodder
Simeon went to Egypt
medium.explanation: The steward first brought them into Joseph’s house and gave them water and fodder; afterward they prepared the present.

medium.question: What does “treasure” mean in “God hath given you treasure in your sacks”?
answers: A hidden valuable thing
A vessel for drinking water
A gift brought to a guest
medium.explanation: The word refers to the money hidden or found in their sacks.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “I had your money”?
answers: The steward had received their payment for the grain
He had never seen their money
Their money had been stolen on the way
challenge.explanation: He said that he had received their money, so he did not expect them to pay again.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Preparing the present, washing their feet, and bringing out Simeon
Bringing out Simeon, bringing the brothers into Joseph’s house, and preparing the present
Eating with Joseph, bringing out Simeon, and giving water
challenge.explanation: Simeon was brought out first; the brothers were then brought into the house and given water and fodder; finally they prepared the present.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers prepare the present before Joseph came?
answers: They knew he would eat with them
They wanted to hide Simeon
They thought Joseph would not come
challenge.explanation: They had heard that they would eat bread there, so they prepared the present in advance.

questions.question: What can be understood from “I had your money”?
answers: The steward had received their payment for the grain
He had never seen their money
Their money had been stolen on the way
questions.explanation: He said that he had received their money, so he did not expect them to pay again.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Preparing the present, washing their feet, and bringing out Simeon
Bringing out Simeon, bringing the brothers into Joseph’s house, and preparing the present
Eating with Joseph, bringing out Simeon, and giving water
questions.explanation: Simeon was brought out first; the brothers were then brought into the house and given water and fodder; finally they prepared the present.

questions.question: Why did the brothers prepare the present before Joseph came?
answers: They knew he would eat with them
They wanted to hide Simeon
They thought Joseph would not come
questions.explanation: They had heard that they would eat bread there, so they prepared the present in advance.

paragraphs.title: Joseph meets Benjamin and breaks down in tears

easy.question: What did the brothers bring Joseph when they came into his house?
answers: The present
Clothing
Money
easy.explanation: The brothers brought Joseph the present that was in their hands.

easy.question: Whom did Joseph ask whether he was still alive?
answers: Benjamin
Their father
One of his servants
easy.explanation: Joseph asked about their elderly father and whether he was still alive.

easy.question: What did Joseph do after deciding to weep?
answers: He left the house
He spoke with the brothers
He entered a room and wept there
easy.explanation: Joseph entered his chamber so that he could weep away from the brothers.

medium.question: Why did Joseph hurry into a room after seeing Benjamin?
answers: His feelings were stirred, and he wanted to weep
He wanted to bring the present
The brothers asked him to leave
medium.explanation: Seeing Benjamin awakened strong emotions in Joseph, so he went to a room to weep.

medium.question: In “his bowels did yearn upon his brother,” what is meant?
answers: He became angry
He felt deep compassion
He felt hungry
medium.explanation: The context shows that seeing Benjamin stirred deep affection and emotion in Joseph.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph wept, saw Benjamin, and then asked about their father
Joseph asked about their father, saw Benjamin, and then entered a room to weep
Joseph entered the room, asked about their father, and then saw Benjamin
medium.explanation: Joseph first asked about their father, then saw Benjamin, and finally entered the room and wept.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph calling Benjamin “his mother’s son”?
answers: Benjamin was his full brother, from the same mother
Benjamin was his brother only through their father
Joseph did not know who Benjamin was
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Joseph and Benjamin shared the same mother, making the meeting especially emotional.

challenge.question: What does the contrast between Joseph’s words to the brothers and his weeping in private show?
answers: Joseph had no interest in his family
Joseph hid his feelings and tried to remain composed
Joseph was angry with Benjamin
challenge.explanation: Joseph spoke formally to the brothers but then hid and wept, showing that he concealed his deep emotions.

challenge.question: Which detail shows Joseph’s special affection for Benjamin?
answers: He asked about everyone in Egypt
He asked for another present
He said to Benjamin, “God be gracious unto thee, my son”
challenge.explanation: Calling Benjamin “my son” and blessing him express warmth and affection.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph calling Benjamin “his mother’s son”?
answers: Benjamin was his full brother, from the same mother
Benjamin was his brother only through their father
Joseph did not know who Benjamin was
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Joseph and Benjamin shared the same mother, making the meeting especially emotional.

questions.question: What does the contrast between Joseph’s words to the brothers and his weeping in private show?
answers: Joseph had no interest in his family
Joseph hid his feelings and tried to remain composed
Joseph was angry with Benjamin
questions.explanation: Joseph spoke formally to the brothers but then hid and wept, showing that he concealed his deep emotions.

questions.question: Which detail shows Joseph’s special affection for Benjamin?
answers: He asked about everyone in Egypt
He asked for another present
He said to Benjamin, “God be gracious unto thee, my son”
questions.explanation: Calling Benjamin “my son” and blessing him express warmth and affection.

paragraphs.title: Joseph restrains himself and begins the meal

easy.question: What did Joseph do at the beginning of the verse?
answers: He washed his face
He ate bread
He went into the field
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And he washed his face.”

easy.question: What did Joseph do after washing his face?
answers: He went to sleep
He went out
He called his brothers
easy.explanation: After washing his face, the verse says, “and went out.”

easy.question: What did Joseph tell them to set on?
answers: Water
Clothing
Bread
easy.explanation: At the end of the verse Joseph said, “Set on bread.”

medium.question: What was the order of Joseph’s actions?
answers: He washed his face, went out, restrained himself, and ordered bread to be served
He went out, ate, washed his face, and restrained himself
He restrained himself, ordered bread, washed his face, and went out
medium.explanation: This is the order in which the verse describes Joseph’s actions.

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask for bread after going out and restraining himself?
answers: To continue the meal
To end the meeting angrily
To go to sleep
medium.explanation: After controlling his emotions, Joseph returned to ordinary conduct and continued the meal.

medium.question: What does “refrained himself” mean in this context?
answers: He restrained and controlled himself
He fell asleep
He hurried to eat
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Joseph controlling his emotions before going out and speaking.

challenge.question: Which detail suggests that Joseph tried to hide or restrain his emotions?
answers: He ordered bread
He washed his face and restrained himself
He went out
challenge.explanation: Washing his face and restraining himself indicate an effort to control his emotions.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph going out before saying, “Set on bread”?
answers: The order about food came after he prepared himself
Joseph refused to eat
Joseph left the house permanently
challenge.explanation: The verse’s order is that Joseph washed, went out, restrained himself, and only then ordered bread.

challenge.question: Which quality of Joseph is especially evident in this verse?
answers: Impatience
Cowardice
Self-control
challenge.explanation: The statement that Joseph restrained himself highlights his self-control.

questions.question: Which detail suggests that Joseph tried to hide or restrain his emotions?
answers: He ordered bread
He washed his face and restrained himself
He went out
questions.explanation: Washing his face and restraining himself indicate an effort to control his emotions.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph going out before saying, “Set on bread”?
answers: The order about food came after he prepared himself
Joseph refused to eat
Joseph left the house permanently
questions.explanation: The verse’s order is that Joseph washed, went out, restrained himself, and only then ordered bread.

questions.question: Which quality of Joseph is especially evident in this verse?
answers: Impatience
Cowardice
Self-control
questions.explanation: The statement that Joseph restrained himself highlights his self-control.

easy.question: Who sat and ate by himself?
answers: Joseph
The brothers
The Egyptians
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph was served by himself.

easy.question: Who ate separately from the Egyptians?
answers: Joseph
The brothers
The Egyptians
easy.explanation: The verse says that the brothers ate by themselves.

easy.question: Why could the Egyptians not eat bread with the Hebrews?
answers: They had no bread
The Hebrews refused to eat
It was an abomination to the Egyptians
easy.explanation: The verse explains that eating with Hebrews was considered an abomination by the Egyptians.

medium.question: How was the eating arranged?
answers: Joseph alone, the brothers alone, and the Egyptians alone
Everyone sat together
Joseph and the Egyptians together, and the brothers alone
medium.explanation: The verse describes three separate groups: Joseph, the brothers, and the Egyptians.

medium.question: What can be understood from the separation of the diners?
